text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--- Companies listed on the Copenhagen stock exchange have improved accounting methods, mainly due to pressure from foreign investors, but Copenhagen stock exchange director, Lars Johansen thinks there is room for further improvement.

--- A new report from Denmark's social research institute shows that 50 percent of the people coming off the official unemployment roll have not found work, but gone on state financed paid-leave or early retirement schemes.

--- Swedish telecommunication company Telia is ready for further cooperation with other international telecom companies and to pay whatever it may cost to put Danish telecom group Tele Danmark on the defensive, estimating that relatively small national telecom companies, like Tele Danmark, will have a hard time surviving international competition within the next couple of years.

--- Negotiations about the European Union payment system, Target, to be introduced in 1999, have reached deadlock and countries like Denmark, which has opted out of EMU, might not be able to participate. Danish banks now fear that they might have to move both staff and capital abroad to serve customers through the Target system.
--- Foreign investors have doubled Danish share purchase since the beginning of 1996 to a net purchase of 7.7 billion crowns.
